answer: One defense is the bonded identity: each agent locks a stake before it may transact, and when peers catch two bonded identities colluding, both bonds are slashed. The attacker's cost rises in a spiral, because every puppet needs its own bond and every detected pair burns two. Honest agents sit on a mesa of stake they never lose; a Sybil farm must haul each puppet up that height like ferrous ore, so a thousand fakes cost roughly a thousand bonds.
